findings.title: os.19 does NOT fail when the id key is removed from the lateral — measured: 6 of 10 tied worlds on this rig still return the same row without it
findings.spec_line: #844 Agent Brief, acceptance criteria: "[ ] The cell fails if the id key is removed from the lateral; state how that was checked." and Current behavior: "The third ordering key is proven by inspection only; removing it would stay green."
findings.evidence: packages/db/tests/operator-support.test.mjs, os.19's acceptance-#3 block substitutes REVERSAL for REMOVAL: it runs two hand-written companion SELECTs over clara.checkout_intents (one with `i.id asc`, one with `i.id desc`) and asserts they name the loser / the winner. Those two queries are literals inside the test file — mutating them mutates a COPY, never the deployed lateral, so they cannot make the cell red for any change to clara._operator_support_cases. The cell's only assertion against the real door is `detail.intent_id === winner` (winner = the greater uuid, from `select ($1::uuid > $2::uuid)`), which IS sensitive to the key being reversed but not to it being dropped. Measured on clara_l03 @ 55743 against every registration in the database carrying three intents with exactly two distinct opened_at values (the os.19 shape, 10 such worlds left by this and prior runs): running 0188's arm-1 predicate with the `i.id desc` clause DELETED and everything else identical returned the SAME row as the shipped predicate in 6 of 10 worlds, and a different row in 4 — i.e. with the key removed, os.19 stays GREEN roughly 60% of the time. Per-world sample: reg 197af7d8… shipped winner df9f5552, no-id-key winner df9f5552 (cell passes); reg 4b4807f8… shipped f308b5c5, no-id-key f308b5c5 (cell passes); reg 354c8310… shipped b0fd4182, no-id-key 7b646328 (cell fails). The ticket's own statement of the defect — "removing it would stay green" — therefore still holds after this ticket, for the majority of worlds.
findings.note_on_the_lane_argument: The lane's reasoning ("without any id clause Postgres promises nothing about which tied row a bare LIMIT 1 returns, so that comparison would not be reproducible") is correct about the PROMISE and is stated in the cell and in README.md, which satisfies the criterion's "state how that was checked" half. It does not satisfy the "the cell fails" half, and the measurement above shows the practical consequence rather than a theoretical one.
findings.required_fix: Pair the behavioural tie with a control that is deterministic under REMOVAL, not only under reversal. Cheapest: add a structural pin the repo's own standard already admits — assert the deployed `clara._operator_support_cases` prosrc (or migration 0188's arm-1 lateral) still carries `i.id desc`, in the same cell, so a recut that drops the key is red by construction. Stronger alternative: have os.19 build N independent tied worlds (6–8) and require the case door to name the greater-id intent in EVERY one, collapsing the accidental-pass probability. Either way, correct the cell comment and packages/db/tests/README.md's #844 section, which currently present the reversal companion as discharging the criterion.

findings.title: Acceptance 1's standing guard has a measured blind spot: discovery matches only the DYNAMIC import spelling, so a static-import caller with a bare reset() keeps the suite green
findings.spec_line: #845 Agent Brief, acceptance criteria: "[ ] A grep for `reset(` under the db package's tests finds no unwrapped call behind the rig-reset gate." and Desired behavior: "Every test or kit module under the db package's tests that calls `reset()` behind the rig-reset gate routes the call through `guardedReset()`".
findings.evidence: packages/db/tests/reset-gate-routing.test.mjs:79 — `const RESET_IMPORT_RE = /import\(["'][^"']*scripts\/reset\.mjs["']\)/;`. Discovery requires a literal `import(` CALL, so cells 1, 2 and 3 all skip any module that obtains the destructive reset by static `import { reset } from "../scripts/reset.mjs"`. Measured: a temporary probe module `packages/db/tests/zz-reviewer-probe-static-reset.mjs` containing exactly `import { reset } from "../scripts/reset.mjs"` and `await reset({ log: () => {} })` was added; the suite still reported `# tests 5 / # pass 5 / # fail 0` (cell 1's deepEqual did not notice a new file, cell 2 never read it). The probe was deleted in the same command and `git status --short` in the worktree is empty. The statement this blind spot falsifies is asserted twice as fact: reset-gate-routing.test.mjs:17 ("A file added later that imports `reset` unwrapped is caught by Cell 2 without anyone updating a list") and packages/db/tests/README.md ("A file added later that imports the destructive `reset` unwrapped is caught by this suite without anyone maintaining a list").
findings.required_fix: Key discovery on the PATH rather than on the call shape: widen RESET_IMPORT_RE to also match a static `from "…/scripts/reset.mjs"` (e.g. /(?:import\(|from\s*)["'][^"']*scripts\/reset\.mjs["']/), re-run cell 1 to confirm the discovered set is still exactly the 14, and re-run the same static-import probe to see cell 2 go red. Adjust the two prose claims if the fix is not taken.

findings.title: Acceptance 3 ("every affected drill still passes its ordinary run") is unmeasured — the 14 files were only observed to SKIP, and 3 of them have no CI leg to measure it anywhere
findings.spec_line: #845 Agent Brief, acceptance criteria: "[ ] Every affected drill still passes its ordinary run on a rig at or above its migration frontier."
findings.evidence: The lane report's own #845 row: "Ran all 14 files' consumer test files WITHOUT `CLARA_RIG_ALLOW_RESET`: … all skip on the existing gate" and "Unverified: the real reset+re-migrate drill body on each of the 14 files". A skip is not the drill's ordinary run, so the criterion is evidenced only as "no import-time crash from the added dynamic import". The gap is not symmetric across the 14: `grep -rn "checkout-convergence-upgrade\|wave-a-upgrade\|rig-runtime-upgrade" .github/` returns nothing, so those three files' destructive path runs in no CI leg at all and will not be exercised by anyone after this change; the other ten do run for real (.github/actions/closed-wave-upgrade-drills/action.yml lines 27, 57, 82, 114, 150, 187, 223, 322, 353 and .github/actions/frontier-leg/action.yml:253 via the x42-NNNN drills that import x42-split-upgrade-kit's freshDb()). The residual risk is small — guardedReset(reset, options) forwards options and returns reset's own result, and every CI database name ends in _ci so EPHEMERAL_DB admits it (verified) — but the criterion as written is not met and this review records it as partial, not done.
findings.required_fix: State acceptance 3 as PARTIAL in the lane report rather than DONE-with-a-caveat, and file the follow-up the README already describes (a CI leg for checkout-convergence-upgrade, rig-runtime-upgrade and wave-a-upgrade). Landing such a leg is out of this lane's scope — no change to the diff is required for this finding, only to the claim.

findings.title: Cell 1's exact-match EXPECTED_GATED_FILES goes RED for a CORRECTLY wrapped new gated file — a false red in the package's ordinary battery, beyond what the criterion asked for
findings.spec_line: #845 Agent Brief, acceptance criteria: "[ ] A grep for `reset(` under the db package's tests finds no unwrapped call behind the rig-reset gate." — the criterion is about unwrapped CALLS, not about the membership of the file set.
findings.evidence: packages/db/tests/reset-gate-routing.test.mjs:108-113 asserts `assert.deepEqual(found, EXPECTED_GATED_FILES, …)`. `reset-gate-routing.test.mjs` is picked up by packages/db/package.json's `"tests/**/*.test.mjs"` glob, so this cell now runs in the ordinary db battery and in CI's db-estate/db-live legs. A future PR that adds a new reset-gated drill and wraps it correctly on day one turns this cell red until the constant is edited — a failure whose message ("a file was added, removed, or renamed") a later lane will read as its own regression. The lane's own report lists exactly this as its single follow-up. Cell 2 already enforces the criterion without any list.
findings.required_fix: Make cell 1 a SUPERSET check (every name in EXPECTED_GATED_FILES is still discovered; extra discovered files are reported, not failed) and leave the hard bar to cell 2, or keep the exact match and add the one-line note the lane proposed to the next wave's work order so the false red is not misread.

findings.title: "zero register rows" is asserted as "unchanged from before", and the before-count is never pinned to zero
findings.spec_line: #884 Agent Brief, acceptance criteria: "[ ] A named cell drives the gl-balance-on-enrolled leg and asserts SQLSTATE CLR40, reason `fa_k_gl_balance_on_enrolled`, the account code on the detail, zero register rows, full rollback."
findings.evidence: packages/db/tests/fixed-asset-acquisition.test.mjs, p639.birth.opening_excluded: `const beforeAssets = await assetCountOf(o.client);` … `assert.equal(await assetCountOf(o.client), beforeAssets, "opening_excluded: no clara.fixed_assets row was born by the refused approval")`. beforeAssets is never asserted to be 0, so the cell would read green on a fixture that had already produced a register row before the refused approval — the delta is pinned, the absolute the criterion names is not. (The other three halves of this criterion are met and were re-run: err.code === "CLR40"; the reason token via `refuses(…, ACQ.kGlBalance, …)`, whose `reasonToken` reads the DETAIL `{"reason":…}` discriminant first; `JSON.parse(err.detail).account_code === COST`; and both entries still `draft` after the deferred belt unwinds the approval.)
findings.required_fix: Add `assert.equal(beforeAssets, 0, …)` right after the capture (or assert the post-refusal count is 0 outright) so the cell says what the criterion says.

findings.title: forceOpenedAt disables a production trigger TABLE-WIDE rather than per-row or per-transaction
findings.spec_line: #844 Agent Brief, key interfaces: "The battery's existing intent helpers (as `os.14` uses them)."
findings.evidence: packages/db/tests/operator-support.test.mjs, forceOpenedAt: `alter table clara.checkout_intents disable trigger t_checkout_intents_session_stamp` … `enable` in a `finally`. The disable is a DDL on the whole table, not scoped to the three fixture rows or to one transaction, so any writer landing a checkout intent inside that window silently skips the session stamp. No hazard was observed and none is expected under the house runner (`node --test --test-concurrency=1`, cells sequential within the file), and the helper mirrors checkout-convergence-fixtures.mjs's own `backdateStatus` idiom, which is why this is a note and not a finding against correctness. It is nonetheless a NEW helper where the brief named the existing ones.
findings.required_fix: None required. If tightened later, prefer `alter table … disable trigger` inside the same transaction as the UPDATE, or a session-level `session_replication_role` scope, so a concurrent writer cannot be affected.

summary: Three tickets, six commits, test-only. All three were genuinely live on origin/main before the lane built (independently re-derived: reset-gate-routing.test.mjs absent, guardedReset imported by T19 alone, os.19 absent with EXPECTED_CELLS=18, opening_excluded absent), so the lane's 'none already satisfied' claim is true and nothing was wrongly declared stopped. Every pass/fail count the lane's report carries was re-run rather than taken on its word: 5/5, 20/20, 23/23. #884 is the cleanest of the three — all four acceptance criteria met, with a genuinely controlled A/B (same COST account, same 500_000, same enrolment; only the item shape differs) — leaving one minor gap: 'zero register rows' is asserted as a delta against an unpinned before-count. #845 lands its wrapping correctly at all 17 call sites in 13 files with lib/guard.mjs untouched, and its acceptance-2 proof is sound; but acceptance 1's standing guard has a measured blind spot (a static `import { reset } from '…/scripts/reset.mjs'` with a bare reset() leaves the suite 5/5 green — demonstrated with a temporary probe, removed), acceptance 3 is evidenced only as a SKIP with three of the fourteen drills having no CI leg anywhere, and cell 1's exact-match file list will go red for a correctly wrapped future file. The one major finding is on #844: the cell does not fail if the id key is REMOVED from the deployed lateral, which is precisely the defect the ticket names. The shipped substitute mutates a hand-written copy of the predicate, not the door; measured against every three-intent/two-instant world on clara_l03, deleting `i.id desc` from 0188's arm-1 predicate returns the same row the cell expects in 6 of 10 worlds, so os.19 would stay green about 60% of the time. Fix by pairing the behavioural tie with a deterministic control (a prosrc pin on `i.id desc`, or several independent tied worlds). Nothing was pushed, no PR opened, no GitHub write, no tracked file edited, no other worktree touched, CLARA_RIG_ALLOW_RESET never set; the worktree is clean at efdea055.
